title: Distributions, random state and Monte Carlo evidence
outcome: Use explicit random generators, compare simulation with analytic quantities and preserve the distinction between numerical and sampling uncertainty.

exercises.title: State the parameterization
exercises.hint: The second argument is standard deviation.
exercises.answer: A familiar parameter name should be checked against the actual distribution API.

exercises.title: Reproduce a sequence
exercises.task: Create two generators with the same seed and sample the same distribution.
exercises.expected: They produce equal arrays in the stated runtime.
exercises.answer: This demonstrates reproducibility under the current implementation, not a universal cross-version promise.

exercises.title: Advance the generator
exercises.task: Draw twice from one generator object.
exercises.expected: Its state advances and the arrays differ in the fixture.
exercises.hint: A seed initializes state; it is not reapplied on every call.
exercises.answer: Reusing or recreating a generator defines different sampling procedures.

exercises.title: Scale Monte Carlo work
exercises.task: Increase the draw count by a factor of 4 under independent sampling.
exercises.expected: The theoretical mean standard-error scale halves.
exercises.hint: Use sigma divided by square root of n.
exercises.answer: An individual realization can still deviate unpredictably; the scaling is a statement about the sampling model.

exercises.title: Inspect an extreme tail
exercises.task: Compare a survival-function calculation with naive subtraction.
exercises.expected: A stable tail API retains a small positive probability.
exercises.hint: Avoid cancellation before taking a logarithm.
exercises.answer: Probability APIs have different numerical roles even when algebraic formulas look equivalent.

exercises.title: Interpret the plot
exercises.task: Compare empirical frequencies with the exact Binomial masses.
exercises.expected: Finite simulated frequencies fluctuate around the model probabilities.
exercises.hint: Keep the sample size and model assumptions visible.
exercises.answer: The chart is a mechanism demonstration and does not establish a real population distribution.
